Move at high speeds by touching and\nholding the Battle Skill button and\ninvoking a Charge Assault.
Using Battle Skills will\ndeplete your AP.
AP can be recovered over time or by\nunleashing regular attacks.
Players that create Multiplayer lobbies are\nrewarded with Host Bonuses.
The more players that participate in the\nMultiplayer, the larger the Host Bonus.
Once you borrow a character, you will not\nbe able to do so again for some time.
When participating as a Guest in a\nMultiplayer battle, your Stamina\nwill not be depleted.
Upon clearing a Mission for the first time,\nyou will be given an Initial Clear Reward.
Missions cannot be cleared by\nparticipating as a Guest in a\nMultiplayer battle.
Occasionally, you will fight Surprise Battles\nwherein random enemies will join the fight.
Mission Tickets will only allow you access\nto a Mission once.
When your Rush Gauge is full, you can\nunleash a powerful Rush Mode ability.
You can chain Rush Mode abilities\ntogether to make up to 4-move combos.
Tap on an allied character's icon during\nbattle to change your primary character.
Regular attacks do different things at\nshort and long distances.
Invoking a character's Talents is a\npowerful way to change the tides of\nbattle and attain victory.

Only the Host can decide to Continue a
Multiplayer battle. Should they choose
to do so, all participants will revive
with full health.
Attackers launch melee attacks to topple\nclose-range enemies.
Defenders are excellent at absorbing\ndamage and taking the heat off the\nrest of the party.
Sharpshooters launch ranged attacks and\nwipe out enemies from a distance.
Invokers use Symbology to deal damage\nto enemies in a certain radius.
Healers use Symbology to recover allies'\nHP and remove status ailments.
During battle, flick the screen to evade,\nwhich will expend AP.
You can also change targets during battle\nby tapping on the enemy you want to\nattack.
When Poisoned, your HP will continually\nbe reduced.
When Frozen, you will move more slowly\nand all non-ice attacks will deal you\ncritical damage.
When Paralyzed, you will be unable to\nperform any actions.
When Silenced, you will be unable to\ninvoke any Battle Skills.
When Cursed, damage will be dealt to\nyou at regular intervals and interrupt\nyour actions.

Unleashing a chain of attacks on a foe
will make them Enraged. They will move
faster and your attacks will stop
interrupting theirs.
The longer the Rush Mode chain, the\nhigher the Damage Bonus.
All ailments will be removed upon\nprogressing to the next Stage. The only\nexception to this is if you are KO'd.
Story Missions will not consume Stamina,\nso feel free to play through them as often\nas you'd like!
Be sure to have party members who can\ndeal with status ailments.
Check the Events menu for limited-time\nmissions that yield enhancement\nmaterials!
Use the Edit function to select characters\nwith different roles to create a well-\nbalanced Party.
During Multiplayer events, send other\nplayers Stamps to let them know how\nyou're feeling.
Note that you cannot pause during\nMultiplayer battles.
When creating a lobby, you can recruit\nspecific roles.
Players can review Rush Mode ability\ndescriptions by holding the RUSH button\nduring battle.
Try changing affinities if your attacks\ndon't deal much damage.
Damage from critical hits ignores your\nfoe's defenses.
Damage from critical hits ignores your\nfoe's defenses.
Be sure to add a Healer into your Party\nbefore embarking on a Mission with\nmany battles.
Good defenders keep their enemies'\nattention focused on them.
By unleashing a string of Battle Skill\nattacks, you can increase the damage you\ninflict with Cancel Bonuses.
The more consecutive hits you get in,\nthe bigger the Rush Gauge bonus.
Please note that Gems cannot be\npurchased from the Continue screen.
When an off-screen enemy is about to\nunleash an attack, their cursor will\nglow red.
Stun enemies by pelting them with\nelemental attacks.
The factor "Grit" will occasionally save\nyour character from being KO'd.
Healing symbology spell targets are\nchosen automatically.
Unlock the next floor in the Maze of\nTribulations by clearing the previous one!
The Maze of Tribulations is comprised of\nfixed floors and a dungeon with\nlimited time only missions.

Spacedate 539
  A federation hybrid research vessel 
meets with tragedy on its return 
from reconnaissance when it is 
assailed by pirates.
As the vessel continues to take 
damage, its captain makes the 
courageous decision to engage their
subspace warp drive. The attempt
fails, however, and the ship
disappears in a flash of light.
  The captain awakens in an
unknown sector far outside the
federation's jurisdiction. As the 
captain scouts out their unintended 
destination, they stumble upon a girl 
being chased by a vicious beast.
  In an attempt to help her, the 
captain joins the fight, but all 
seems in vain...until the mysterious 
stranger uses something akin to 
summoning symbology to 
materialize an ally.
This newfound companion proves
integral in enabling them to escape 
into orbit around the planet.
  Though their journey ahead will
doubtless be long and their energy
so low that they cannot power
even their shields, what weighs on
the captain's mind the most is the
strange powers possessed by the
girl in white they found.

The crew lands on the planet
Maere seeking provisions, but finds
little help, as something there is
jamming their ship's sensors. With
little recourse, the captain and
Evelysse set out to find the source
of their ails.
  They discover that a tower is
emitting those pesky signals, but
what is a structure that disrupts
sensors doing on so primitive a
planet? The answer to this question
seems to be that an illicit mining
operation has been erected on
fringe planets, something that
angers Eve to no end.
  The crew vows to save as many
planets as they can from the same
fate that befell Maere, meaning their
journey back to Earth may take a
tad longer than anticipated.

A few days after leaving Levarance,
there is a sudden message from Kurt. 
Apparently he's lost contact with Val
and Terry, who were on their way to
Viret to work on dismantling a
pulse tower. 

  Together with a worried Kurt, the
party starts searching the inside of
the pulse tower, which was the
missing pair's last-known location.
All of a sudden, however, the
tower's defense system activates,
bulkheads start to close down,
and a poisonous gas is released
into the air. 

  Having lost contact with Val and
Terry, the party makes a dash for
the nerve center at the heart of
the tower, but they are separated
from Kurt by a closing bulkhead
blocking the path. 

  Fortunately, however, they are rescued
by Val and Terry.

  They learn from their rescuers of
the special abilities Kurt possesses,
and how deeply entwined with
their past the man is. 

  Val is desperately worried about
Kurt, while Kurt powers on at full
speed, single-mindedly heading
for his goal.

  With the tower now in total
lockdown, the two men's wills
come to a head.

The crew finds another planet that
has fallen victim to excavation.
Promptly after touching down, they
realize that―despite the lush
vegetation―the human population
looks to to be on the brink of
extinction.
  In contrast, a perverse ecology of
crystalline-barbed fiends thrives―
and it does not take the explorers
long to label this phenomenon a
side effect of the illegal mining. If
the population of Esperance is to
survive, the source of this thorny
nuisance must be removed.
  The crew does succeed in
eliminating the beast from whence
the spiked horrors spawned, but
the planet remains in shambles.
The explorers can do naught, sadly,
but entrust its well-being to the
locals and continue on their
adventure.

This time, the planet they alight
upon is host to an advanced
civilization, but that hardly means
the world is free from tumult.
  A group of self-proclaimed
freedom fighters greets the party,
but the actions of these rebels
seem anything but altruistic. As
the travelers try to ascertain what
these brigands' motives are, they
learn that a group called The Purge
is behind the excavations. Moreover,
the jamming towers are a means by
which they can extract precious
metals from these unsuspecting
host planets. The metals' purpose,
however, remains shrouded in
mystery.
   The crew manages to find the
man who shared this vile technology
with the Esperancians and corner
him...or so they thought, as he
transports away in the blink of an
eye, leaving the group feeling irked
and defeated.

Soon after the crew repairs their
communication system, they arrive 
at a tranquil planet that Evelysse 
dubs "Pasithee." Though their sensors
are jammed yet again, the crew receives
a garbled transmission from the surface, 
and sets out to search the planet.
  This time, there is not one tower
doing the jamming, but three. During
their deactivation exploits, they
finally locate the person who sent
the transmission―or at least the
recording of his voice that has
been playing for years.
  The recording mentions something
about "Operation: Frost," but the
crew has little else to go on and
is forced to set off once again.

Somehow, the ship's navigation
system fails to register an
immense collection of cosmic debris
that lies between them and their
destination. The crew reasons that
circumnavigating it, however,
would likely take an exceedingly
long time, so they opt to charge
headlong through the mass of
detritus.
  As they do, the explorers find
a wrecked Purge ship―along with a
way to decrypt the data they
obtained on Maere. It reveals the
specifics of Operation: Frost―an
absurd and degenerate plan to put
whole planets into cryogenic stasis.

After emerging from that tract of
debris, the crew visits a craggy
desert of a world. It too has been
ravaged by the Purge, to the point
where its mantle and core are
riddled with gargantuan caverns.
  Amidst fears that they will fall
to one of the planet's endless
quakes, the crew decides to leave...
until Eve tries one last thing in
order to save it.
  Crisis is averted thanks to her
previously hidden power, but Eve's
abilities breed doubt in Coro's
mind. The onboard AI eventually
relents after being reminded how
selfless Eve has been, but the
group has no time to revel in their
renewed bonds, for they are soon
beset by thornites again.

Their search for members of The
Purge leads the captain and 
Evelysse to the planet Dvaleor, 
where they run into a trio of 
eccentric individuals. Though comical,
these three stooges tell of an 
apocalyptic herald that rendered The 
Purge's home planet of Levarance 
uninhabitable―a disease called the 
"Devil's Plague."
  Furthermore, a man named Eldram
has exploited this pandemic to
consolidate his power and become
dictator of Levarance's people as
they drift from planet to planet,
unwittingly destroying the worlds
from which they harvest metal.
All they knew was that to disobey
Eldram is to invite one's own death.
   Armed with the knowledge of what
their work has wrought, however, the
trio pledges their aid to the 
explorers in overthrowing the tyrant 
Eldram.

With the help of the wacky
Dvaleoran trio, the explorers manage
to reach a Purge laboratory. The
base has already been deserted by
the time they arrive, but they do
meet a child named Verda, who
claims to be the leading authority on
the Devil's Plague.
  As Verda's goal of eradicating the
plague once and for all coincides
with the explorers' mission, she
joins them in their search. She also
informs the group that, as the
facility itself is a target of Operation:
Frost, they had best extract what
information they can before the
place is frozen. While searching for 
data, she tells the crew more about
Levarance and the Devil's Plague,
and explains her most ardent
wish.
  With some data finally retrieved,
the group makes for their ship, but
before they can reach it, the
captain begins to show symptoms
of the plague. Verda laments that
once someone is afflicted with the
disease, they must be put in
cryogenic stasis, but Evelysse seems
to have other ideas, and unleashes
powers the likes of which none have
ever seen.

With the Devil's Plague spreading
like wildfire, the captain resigns
themselves to their fate. But
thanks to Evelysse, they
manage to cheat death. 
  The party heads to Levarance in
order to create a vaccine against
the Devil's Plague, using
antibodies developed in the
captain's immune system. 
  However, a Thornite battalion is
lying in wait. 
  With the help of their comrades,
the party manages to defend the lab
where the vaccine is being
developed, but Eldram, now
aware of the vaccine's existence,
sets a trap. 
  Verda is desperate to make Eldram
explain his motives, but her pleas
fall on deaf ears as he shoots her. 
  Despite grave injuries, Verda is
determined to understand Eldram,
who remains stubbornly taciturn. 
  Verda must complete the vaccine,
so the captain and company fight
through Thornite forces to confront
Eldram. 
  However, awaiting the party beyond
that battle is a new, and even more
sinister threat.
Chilling News in the Riven Ring
Of Old Labs and Young Girls
